jobs.description:
Cloud Operations Engineer to join Global IT department at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you’re energised by cloud technology and working closely with users to solve their challenges and thrive on learning and finding practical solutions, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our dedicated team in Global IT.

As a team, we are responsible for operating and continuously improving our Microsoft Azure environment and the processes surrounding our cloud platform.

This is an early-career role where you will get the opportunity to develop your cloud engineering skills while working with real operational challenges. You will work closely with colleagues, internal users, application teams, and other stakeholders.

A key part of your role will be handling requests and incidents related to our Azure environment, improving operational processes and documentation, and helping ensure that our cloud platform remains structured and easy for our users and teams to work with.

How you might spend your days

As a Cloud Operations Engineer, you’ll be:

• 
Handling and following up on end-user requests and incidents related to our Microsoft Azure environment

• 
Supporting the daily operation of our Azure platform, including troubleshooting cloud infrastructure and platform services

• 
Working with Azure DevOps and supporting deployment, automation, and platform processes

• 
Maintaining and improving operational processes, documentation, and ways of working as the platform evolves

• 
Collaborating with end users, application teams, cloud engineers, and other stakeholders to understand requirements and help turn them into practical solutions

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• 
Curious and motivated to learn more about cloud technology and platform engineering

• 
Comfortable working with end users, colleagues and stakeholders with different technical backgrounds

• 
Willing to take ownership of tasks while also asking for help and learning from more experienced colleagues

• 
Interested in improving processes rather than simply following them when there is a better way of working

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• 
Some practical experience with Microsoft Azure, gained through professional work, internships, education & certifications

• 
Familiarity with Azure DevOps or similar tools used for repositories, pipelines, automation, or work management

• 
An interest in cloud operations and platform engineering, including troubleshooting and supporting users

• 
Good communication skills in written and spoken English and an interest in working with different stakeholders

• 
Experience with or knowledge of Azure Landing Zones, Infrastructure as Code, cloud networking, governance, or identity and access management is a plus, but not a requirement

Life at NNE.

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 7 December 2026.

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Maiken Høst Hansen at +45 30 77 45 61.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

jobs.occupation: AI & Data Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
**Help us bring AI from ambition to reality

**At AGC Biologics, we have reached an exciting point in our AI journey. The governance foundation is in place, several high-value use cases have been identified, and we are now ready to scale the development and deployment of AI solutions across the business.

To support this journey, we are looking for an AI & Data Solutions Engineer who can help turn business challenges into practical and scalable AI solutions.

This role sits within our Global Data, AI & Business Platforms organization and will work at the intersection of business, technology, and innovation. You will collaborate with stakeholders across AGC Biologics, partner with AGC Inc.'s Data Science teams, and contribute directly to the design, development, and deployment of AI-powered solutions that support manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and business operations.

**What You'll Be Doing

**In your first months, you will be involved in several AI initiatives already identified across the organization. Some solutions will be developed together with AGC Inc.'s Data Science teams, while others will be built and deployed directly within AGC Biologics.

Success in this role requires someone who enjoys moving between business discussions and technical implementation. One day you may be meeting with stakeholders to understand a new AI opportunity and define requirements. The next, you may be preparing datasets, working on solution architecture, developing machine learning capabilities, or supporting the deployment of an AI solution into production.

You will work closely with our Data Engineering, Analytics, Solution Architecture, and Digitalization teams and play an important role in ensuring that AI solutions are technically robust, business-relevant, and ready for real-world use.

**What We're Looking For

**We imagine you come from a background in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, or a related field, and have already worked hands-on with building, deploying, or supporting AI and data-driven solutions.

You are comfortable working with technologies such as Python, SQL, Azure, and ideally have exposure to platforms such as Microsoft Fabric and Snowflake. Experience working with machine learning models, AI applications, data pipelines, and data preparation is important, while familiarity with Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, or other emerging AI technologies would be a significant advantage.

Equally important is your ability to work with people. This is a highly business-facing role, and we are looking for someone who can confidently engage stakeholders, translate business needs into technical solutions, and communicate complex concepts in a simple and understandable way.

You enjoy collaboration, challenge assumptions constructively, and thrive in environments where priorities evolve and new opportunities emerge.

**Experience That Will Help You Succeed

**Experience from the pharmaceutical, biotech, or other GxP-regulated industries will be considered a strong advantage. We also welcome candidates coming from manufacturing or production-focused environments where technology, data, and business operations come together to support critical processes.

Whether your background is in AI Engineering, Data Science, Machine Learning, or Data Engineering, what matters most is your ability to combine technical expertise with strong stakeholder engagement and a genuine passion for solving business problems through technology.

**Why AGC Biologics?

**This is an opportunity to join a growing global team where AI is becoming a strategic capability across the organization. You will have the chance to influence how AI is adopted, work with modern technologies, collaborate with colleagues across Europe, Asia, and North America, and contribute to solutions that support the development and manufacturing of therapies that improve patients' lives around the world.

If you are excited by the opportunity to help shape the future of AI at AGC Biologics, we would love to hear from you.

**Interested in Joining Us?

**If you are interested we would like to hear from you.

Applications are screened on an ongoing basis. You do not need to attach a cover letter to your application, but please include a few sentences in you CV about your motivation for applying to this position.

Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark, or the greater Malmø area.

If this sounds like the right challenge for you, we’d love to hear from you. Don’t hesitate to apply, even if you don’t meet every single requirement. The right mindset matters just as much.

Please submit your application through the AGC Biologics careers site. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis.

**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Software Developer
jobs.description:
**Build software at scale. Influence how we build it. Help shape the next generation of development at Dalux.

**Dalux is growing, and we are looking for experienced software developers who want significant technical ownership while continuing to build software hands-on.

You will work on products used by professionals around the world, contribute to architectural and technical decisions, and help us improve how we develop software – including how we use agentic AI to make capable developers more effective.

**Your role

**As an Experienced Software Developer, you will take ownership of complex product and technical problems from idea to production.

You will work in a product team with other developers, a Product Manager, and a Product Designer. We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks by making good technical decisions, improving our architecture and development practices, and sharing knowledge with others.

Your work can include:

• Owning complex features and technical problems end-to-end

• Designing scalable, maintainable solutions and contributing to architectural decisions

• Improving our codebase, tooling, developer workflows, and technical quality

• Driving or contributing to initiatives around DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure, architecture, or developer tooling

• Sparring with and mentoring other developers

• Working closely with Product Management and Design to understand problems and find the right solutions

• Bringing new ideas and technologies into Dalux when they can improve our products or how we build them

We expect experienced developers to have opinions, challenge existing solutions, and be comfortable having their own ideas challenged in return.

**Developing software with agentic AI

**We are significantly increasing our use of agentic AI in software development.

We use and explore AI across the development lifecycle – from understanding problems and navigating codebases to implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review.

We are looking for developers who already use agentic AI as part of their development workflow. The specific tools matter less than how you use them: providing the right context and direction, critically evaluating the output, and knowing when to intervene or take a different approach.

Strong engineering fundamentals remain essential. AI can increase what a capable developer can achieve, but you remain responsible for the architecture, correctness, maintainability, and quality of the software you build.

At Dalux, you will help us take these ways of working further by experimenting, sharing what works, and helping establish effective practices for agentic software development.

**Technologies we work with

**Our platform is built on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS. Our primary technologies include:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• GitHub Copilot

• MSSQL

• Elasticsearch

• AWS

• Optionally, Android / iOS development using .NET MAUI

You may also encounter parts of our C++ codebase.

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to understand and improve complex systems matter more.

**Product development at Dalux

**Our developers do more than implement specifications.

Developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers work together to understand problems and find solutions that balance user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

Our products are relied upon by professionals worldwide, making performance, stability, maintainability, and quality important parts of everyday engineering.

**Your background

**We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT, or a related technical field

• Have strong software engineering fundamentals

• Are comfortable owning complex technical problems and decisions

• Can navigate and improve an established codebase and architecture

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and quality

• Enjoy technical sparring and sharing knowledge with other developers

• Understand the trade-offs between short-term delivery and long-term technical quality

Experience with C#/.NET, Angular, or cloud development is useful, but we do not expect you to match every technology we use.

**What You Can Expect From Dalux

**Dalux is a software company at heart. As an experienced developer, you can expect:

• Significant ownership and real influence on technical solutions

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve engineering practices beyond your immediate product work

• An environment actively investing in agentic AI for software development

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you solve problems

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen. Working together in person is an important part of how we collaborate, share knowledge, and make decisions quickly.

**About Dalux

**Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

We build digital tools that make the construction industry smarter and more efficient. Using our own 3D BIM technology, we develop software used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

**Interested?

**If you want significant technical ownership while helping shape how modern software is developed at Dalux, we would like to hear from you.

**If agentic AI is already part of how you develop software, tell us how you use it – what you delegate, how you validate the result, and where you have found it genuinely useful.

**We recruit continuously and hire multiple experienced developers throughout the year as Dalux grows.

If you have questions about the position, contact IT Talent Acquisition Specialist Sara Nielsen on SNI@dalux.com

jobs.occupation: Postdocs in Endocrinology and Developmental Disruption
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications for post-doctoral fellowships in human endocrinology and developmental disruption from January 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
Two fully funded 1–2-years’ postdoc positions are available at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor David M. Kristensen. The positions involve collaboration with Copenhagen University Hospital – Rigshospitalet, Harvard University (USA) and Inserm (France). The projects will focus on developing and using already established models to understand human endocrinology, disruption of development by xenobiotics and translating such data to human clinical endpoints using prospective cohorts.

Responsibilities and tasks
The work will include research within male and female endocrinology, early development, organotypic culture explants, with focus on understanding novel mechanisms of endocrine disruption during development by specific known chemicals. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of organotypic assays using human and murine tissues. 
• Lead rodent experiments to understand disruption of development. 
• Apply standard molecular approaches to characterize RNA and protein expression in cells and tissue samples.
• Analyse and possibly validate candidate biomarkers relevant to developmental disruption using plasma and other biofluid samples from relevant cohorts or models.
• Contribute with mentoring pre-graduate and PhD students within the focus of the research project.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of research accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals.
• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in developmental biology is required.
• Hands-on experience with classic techniques such as qPCR and Western blotting is required.
• Experience with research in endocrinology and endocrine disruption will be an advantage.

jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invite applications for a tenure-track DIAS Fellow position at Assistant Professor level in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment, with a focus on input-output life cycle assessment methods and big data. Who are we looking for?

The position translates this ambition into a concrete research agenda, because many of the most pressing sustainability questions, such as how consumption in one country drives resource use, emissions and social conditions in another, or how a new technology changes environmental impacts across whole economies, cannot be answered within a single discipline. Industrial ecology addresses these questions by tracing material, energy and monetary flows through global supply chains, drawing on methods and data from engineering, economics and the natural and social sciences. Input-output analysis, built on big data covering production, trade, emissions and resource use and combined with life cycle assessment and material flow analysis, provides the quantitative framework for linking decisions about individual products, technologies and policies to their economy-wide consequences. The Fellow will build this capacity at SDU and use DIAS as a platform to work with researchers in fields such as health, food, energy, economics and political science on questions that cross disciplinary boundaries. Within this ambition, the specific profile is as follows.

We seek an early-career researcher who will advance quantitative sustainability assessment within industrial ecology by developing data-driven environmental-economic and systems models that link global production and consumption to environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. The role includes independent research, research-based teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration across DIAS and the Department, and development of competitive external funding proposals. Relevant research themes include:

·         environmental and material footprinting of global production and consumption systems;

·         development and application of environmentally extended input–output (EEIO) and multi-regional input–output (MRIO) models and databases, including hybrid physical–monetary systems and transparent, reproducible data workflows;

·         hybrid modelling that combines EEIO analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA), material flow analysis (MFA), econometrics or other quantitative methods;

·         applications to food and resource systems, healthcare systems and medical technologies, the circular economy, energy, infrastructure and other societal systems; and

·         scenario, structural decomposition, uncertainty and econometric analysis for sustainability transitions, policy and decision support.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

·         A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

·         A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields.

·         Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

·         Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must:

·         Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of industrial ecology, environmental or ecological economics, environmental science or engineering, sustainability science or a closely related field. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

·         The successful candidate should demonstrate strong competence in EEIO or MRIO analysis, and at least one of the following areas: LCA, MFA, or hybrid modelling; econometric, statistical, or other quantitative methods; and programming, data science, or management of large, heterogeneous datasets.

·         Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries.

·         Be fluent in English.

·         Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

·         Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking.

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.   

The Department of Green Technology

The Department of Green Technology at SDU is a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment focused on developing technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Our research spans environmental chemistry, process engineering, life cycle thinking, and circular systems. We collaborate closely with industry and public stakeholders to ensure real-world impact and relevance.

This position will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering (SDU LCE).

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

SDU LCE uses industrial ecology approaches to reduce environmental impacts and reconcile human development with environmental stewardship. We conduct holistic systems analyses and design studies to characterise and optimise engineering solutions over the long term, considering resource use, energy efficiency, climate and environmental impacts, and economic and socioeconomic performance. jobs.occupation: PhD position Pseudoexon Splicing: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Modulation
jobs.description:
The RNA Precision Medicine Center, Section of Translational Biology, at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, the University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a PhD student position within the field of pre-mRNA splicing and disease. The position is to be filled from 1 January, 2027.

The candidate will be part of a dynamic research group, which focus on generating a better understanding of all aspects of RNA biology in human disease and how to translate this into precision medicine.
The present project is focused on pre-mRNA splicing regulatory mechanisms and how inherited mutations can cause aberrant splicing and human disease. 

More specifically, the project will investigate a new strategy for increasing expression by modulating alternative splicing of pseudoexons (PEs) in the 5′ untranslated region (5′ UTR). The project will identify SSO-modulable 5′ UTR PEs in human disease genes, focusing on CNS genes. 

In parallel, the project will investigate how disease-associated variants located upstream of coding regions may cause disease. The project aims to provide mechanistic insight into 5′ UTR splicing and uORF mediated regulation and identify specific SSO-based therapeutic opportunities. Finally, the project should establish a tool to predict pathogenic effects of upstream non-coding variants, thereby improving molecular diagnostics in clinical genetics.
Overall, the project will generate basic knowledge on RNA-centered molecular mechanisms, the molecular pathology of aberrant splicing and it aims at translating this into new precision RNA medicine.

Applications are sought from candidates with a master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, medicine or a related field and documented experience in molecular and cellular biology. 

Specifically, experimental expertise in RNA biology, including working with antisense oligonucleotides and RNA binding small molecule drugs for modulation of splicing, as well as hands-on experience with Next Generation Sequencing technologies and bioinformatics is preferable.
Applicants should have demonstrated scientific productivity, good inter-personal and communication skills, good written and spoken English skills and be able to conduct independent and creative research.

The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology offers a strong, international and competitive research environment within the fields of RNA biology, molecular genetics and cell biology, protein chemistry and mass spectrometry, molecular microbiology and biophysics.

jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (BMB), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), Odense, invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship within the field of membrane biophysics and antifungal drug research. The project, Development and validation of novel antifungal polyene macrolides, will be carried out in the group of Daniel Wüstner. The position is to be filled from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project
Fungal infections are a growing threat to human health, and only few classes of antifungal drugs are available. Polyene macrolides such as nystatin, natamycin and amphotericin B act by interacting with ergosterol, the main sterol of fungal membranes, but their precise mode of action is still poorly understood. This limits the rational design of new, more selective and less toxic polyenes.
The aim of this PhD project is to develop and validate novel antifungal polyene macrolides. The PhD student will characterize how new polyene variants interact with sterol-containing model membranes and with living yeast cells. Key methods include UV-sensitive and quantitative fluorescence microscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and biophysical assays of membrane permeability, etc. The project will be carried out in close collaboration with national and international partners.

Your profile
You have a master's degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, chemistry or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with documented experience in:

• 
Fluorescence microscopy

• 
Fluorescence and/or absorption spectroscopy

• 
Working with model membranes, such as liposomes or giant unilamellar vesicles

Experience with yeast as a model organism will be considered an advantage.
You are a team player with a positive attitude, and at the same time you are able to work independently and take responsibility for your own project. Good communication skills and good written and spoken English are required.

Your tasks

• 
Carry out your own research project and present the results in scientific papers and a PhD thesis

Take part in teaching activities at the department

Follow PhD courses as part of the PhD programme

• 
Present your work at national and international conferences

• 
Contribute to the daily life and collaborations of the research group

You will join a dedicated research group with access to state-of-the-art fluorescence microscopy and spectroscopy, and a network of national and international collaborators.

jobs.occupation: Two-Year Novo Nordisk Foundation-funded Postdoc Position in Metabolic Signalling and Adipose Tissue Proteostasis
jobs.description:
Are you a creative and motivated postdoc ready to uncover novel, therapeutically exploitable mechanisms in cardiometabolic disease?
Then join our dynamic research team to lead a groundbreaking project at the intersection of adipose tissue biology, cell signalling, in vivo physiology and obesity therapeutics! 

We are seeking a talented postdoctoral fellow to join us at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark, in Odense. 

This two-year position is funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, with a flexible start from 1.2.2027 and the possibility of extension in case of incurring follow-up funding.

The PRO-METeus project: 
Our lab is exploring a new frontier in endocrinology: Sheddokines. 
These are fragments of cell-surface proteins that are proteolytically cleaved and released to function as atypical hormones, orchestrating communication between adipose tissue and metabolic organs. 
We have compelling evidence that this regulatory network is altered in obese rodents and patients, and the PRO-METeus project aims to identify novel sheddokines and their protease regulators to understand their role in health and disease. Your project will be to help decipher this complex signalling language, paving the way for new sheddokine-targeted therapies for cardiometabolic disorders. 

As our next postdoctoral fellow, you will:

• 
Identify protein fragments released from human and mouse adipocytes.

• 
Validate these candidates in vivo by manipulating their secretion in mouse models of cardiometabolic disease using adipocyte-specific AAVs.

• 
Decipher the molecular mechanisms that regulate shadowiness and their impact on inter-organ communication.

Collectively, PRO-METeus offers a unique opportunity to blend discovery proteomics with functional validation, directly translating your findings into potential therapeutic strategies.

We are seeking an ambitious and passionate postdoctoral researcher eager for discovery. The ideal candidate will have:

• 
A PhD in molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, physiology, or a related field, supported by a strong first-author publication.

• 
A solid background in protein biochemistry and/or cell signalling.

• 
Hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture and standard molecular biology techniques.

• 
Practical experience with metabolic flux assays including Seahorse extracellular flux analysis, and functional cellular readouts.

• 
Experience in proteomic and transcriptomic approaches.

• 
Experience with bioinformatics analysis, including the processing, interpretation and integration of omics datasets.

• 
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Desirable experience includes:

• 
Working with mouse models of cardiometabolic disease.

• 
A background in chromatin biology and gene regulation.

• 
Familiarity with AAV biology and viral-mediated gene delivery.

Our Lab & What We Offer:
You'll be joining a prolific and internationally recognised research group focused on gene regulation, physiology, epigenetic and adipose tissue biology (Kornfeld Nature 2013, Oliverio Nature Cell Biology 2016, Awazawa Nature Medicine 2017, Schmidt Nature Communications 2018, Pradas-Juni Nature Communications 2020, Park Nature Metabolism 2021, Engelhard iScience 2023, Khani-Topel Nature Metabolism 2024, Kaul Nature Metabolism 2025).

We provide:  

• 
A supportive and collaborative research environment.

• 
Access to state-of-the-art facilities for proteomics, molecular biology, and in vivo studies.

• 
Dedicated mentorship and career development, including support for grant writing and presenting at international conferences.

• 
A competitive salary and benefits package in accordance with Danish regulations.

• 
Affiliation with the NNF Centre for Adipocyte Signalling, which uses a holistic, multimodal approach to understand adipocyte dysfunction.
